murna_01.text:
yo Viewer...
this Halima's line right?

look i know this is weird but... she gone.

not ghosted gone
not “i’ll be back in 5” gone
gone gone.

choices.text: What do you mean she’s gone?

murna_who.text:
chill. it’s Murna.
class clown. spiritual dropout.
carries a butter-knife katana and a few shiny rings.

remember me now?

i jacked her phone after the trail ran cold.
she woulda wanted you in.

you’re that Righteous sightseer type, right?
maybe you can see what i can't.

murna_gone.text:
gone as in “wiped off the map.”
bounty job she picked up got real weird.
name wiped from the Nexus network.
no aura trails. no surveillance threads.

it’s like she un-existed.

i jacked her phone after the trail ran cold.

you’re that Righteous sightseer type, right?
maybe you can see what i can't.

murna_last.text:
last ping we got was a warehouse near the Yelwa border.
smelled off.
like... copper and sugar.

found these weird skin flakes and chains.
she was fighting something that didn't bleed right.

i jacked her phone after the trail ran cold.

you’re that Righteous sightseer type, right?
maybe you can see what i can't.

murna_what_happened.text:
bounty job she picked up got real weird.
name wiped from the Nexus network.
no aura trails. no surveillance threads.

it’s like she un-existed.

found these skin flakes and chains.
she was fighting something that didn’t bleed right.

if that ain’t spooky, she left this on her voice recorder:

“They don’t like sunlight. Or prayers. Or names.”

what kinda bounty says that?

murna_why_you.text:
look… she’s really gone.

but before she vanished, she dropped your name.
not like a “help me” kind of drop.
more like…

“if anything happens to me, you find the viewer.”

and now here i am.

choices.text: How do you even know who I am?

murna_how_know.text:
called in a favor.
had Kelvin look you up.

you know how he is — digital messiah with a God-complex and bad sleep habits.

said you and him “already go back.”
his words. not mine.

murna_why_trust.text:
no clue.

but she did.
and that’s enough for me.

Kelvin vouched for you too.
said you and him “already go back.”
his words. not mine.

murna_never.text:
true.

but i know of you.
and Kelvin knows you.

he called you “already go back” people.
his words. not mine.

murna_help_prompt.text:
anyway.

i’m gonna follow what leads i got.
you just do what you do best.
look. see.

tell me where the path twists before i walk into another trap.

cool?

choices.text: I’ll help. Keep feeding me data.
I need more details before I commit.

system_next_morning.text:
[SYSTEM — Next Morning]
Your phone lights up at 06:41.

kelvin_intro.text:
KELVIN:
morning.
hope Murna didn’t scare you off.

choices.text: He went radio silent all night.
You two really need to work on communication.

kelvin_data.text:
KELVIN:
yeah… he’s allergic to teamwork.

but the data you fed him last night was solid.

i’m tracking movement on the border cameras — no aura, no ID tags.
thing is…

the figure matches the height & gait of whoever was with Halima in that warehouse footage.

kelvin_clip.text:
KELVIN:
sending now.

[📹 CLIP — 04 sec — Border Crossing Cam]
Low-res, black & white.
Figure walks stiffly, dragging something wrapped in cloth.

For a fraction of a second, its head turns toward the camera — eyes glint pale.

Then it blurs out of frame.

murna_following.text:
MURNA:
saw that.
following.

warehouse trail → dry creek bed → old tunnel.

Kelvin, patch me in if you catch heat signatures.

pitch_intro.text:
KELVIN:
viewer, meet Pitch.

PITCH:
so you’re the “eyes.”
don’t slow me down.

i’m not here for your little trust exercises — i’m here to drag Murna back before he gets himself eaten.

choices.text: If you’re with Kelvin, I trust you.

pitch_reply_1.text:
PITCH:
hm.
polite.
rare for people Kelvin vouches for.

pitch_reply_2.text:
PITCH:
don’t.
trust makes you sloppy.

pitch_reply_3.text:
PITCH:
good.
keep it that way.

kelvin_wrap.text:
KELVIN:
alright, let’s move.

i’ll feed both of you coordinates as soon as i pin Murna’s trail.

viewer, you’ll get visuals first.
use that Sight.

…tell me what i’m really looking at.
